_comment: Tier-2 for skfem time_dependent#1, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: Crank-Nicolson is 2nd order but oscillates -- 10-30% over/undershoot at sharp transients that does NOT damp with mesh refinement, and switching to theta=1 removes it. Ran: heat equation with a square-pulse IC on MeshTri.init_tensor at n = 16/32/64, ElementTriP1, homogeneous Dirichlet, ten steps, at dt/h^2 = 0.5, 5 and 50 for theta=0.5 and theta=1 (18 runs). Printed: backward Euler's worst undershoot across all nine cases is 0.000002 -- rounding level, more than a thousand times below Crank-Nicolson's smallest (0.026413) -- so theta=1 really does remove the ringing. At a FIXED dt/h^2 the CN undershoot does not damp under refinement (0.2135/0.4429/0.4250 at ratio 5; 0.6442/0.8582/0.7467 at ratio 50), confirming that half of the claim. THE 10-30% BAND IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE SCHEME: on one mesh the undershoot runs from 0.0365 at dt/h^2 = 0.5 to 0.8582 at dt/h^2 = 50, a 23x span, so the governing quantity is dt/h^2 and the test must be for a negative minimum rather than a percentage. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 applies the entry's own remedy at the pathology site - CN_THETA, the theta used by the nine runs tagged 'cn', becomes 1.0 (backward Euler) instead of 0.5, so those runs stop ringing. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 takes cn_min_undershoot_over_all_cases from 0.026413 to -0.000000 (no undershoot at all) and removes 'be_undershoot_below_cn_by_gt_1000x=True', 'cn_always_undershoots=True', 'cn_undershoot_spans_more_than_10x=True' and raises the forbidden 'FAIL:', so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
